profile.summary: PLM-GraphDTA keeps the drug side of GraphDTA, a graph neural network over the molecule, and replaces its protein encoder with a fixed embedding taken from a protein language model. One vector per protein is computed in advance, projected by a small stack of linear layers, concatenated with the drug vector and sent through dense layers to one affinity value. It is the code behind a study comparing many protein embedding types, so the embedding source is a command line choice rather than part of the model.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The drug is a molecular graph with 78 features per atom, encoded by one of four GraphDTA style networks, here GIN, GAT, GAT_GCN or GCN, pooled by summation and projected to a 128 wide vector. The protein is not read as a sequence at all: a precomputed embedding, one vector per protein, is loaded from a json file and passed through linear layers with batch normalisation and ReLU, whose widths are set by the plm_layers argument. The two vectors are concatenated and sent through dense layers of 1024 and 256 units to a single output, trained with mean squared error and Adam. The input width of the protein branch is read from the embedding file itself, so changing the embedding type changes the first layer.
sections.source_locator: models/plm_ginconv.py: PLM_GINConvNet; training.py: embedding loading, optimiser

sections.title: Protein embeddings and splits
sections.body: The protein_embedding_type argument lists the embeddings the study compares: esm_320, esm_640, esm_1280, esmc_960, esmc_1152, deepfri_bp, deepfri_cc, deepfri_ec, deepfri_mf and prost_1024, with the number being the embedding width. The ESM script in the repository loads esm2_t30_150M_UR50D, takes the last layer's token representations and averages them over the residues to give one vector per protein. The repository also ships the fold files for several split regimes: setting1, drug_cold_1 to 5, protein_cold_1 to 5 and fully_blind_1 to 5, for the davis, davis_mutation and kiba datasets.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: There is one code release and no published weights. The repository has no README and no licence file, and the GitHub API returns a null licence field. What a result must name is therefore the run configuration: the model (PLM_GINConvNet, PLM_GATNet, PLM_GAT_GCN, PLM_GCNNet, and the plain GraphDTA and ESM_GATNet baselines the script also imports), the dataset, the embedding type, the plm_layers widths, the fold setting and the seed. Seeding is implemented: with a seed given, the script sets deterministic algorithms and turns cudnn benchmarking off. Training runs 1000 epochs at batch size 512 and saves the model at the best training loss, then evaluates that model on the held out fold.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Five GIN convolution layers of width 32 over the drug graph (or the GAT, GAT_GCN or GCN variant), sum pooling to a 128 wide vector; a protein branch of linear layers with batch normalisation over the precomputed embedding, default width 128; concatenation, then dense layers of 1024 and 256 units to one output.

strengths.text: The protein representation is a plug: ten embedding types are selectable on the command line, from three ESM-2 widths through ESM Cambrian and DeepFRI function embeddings to ProstT5, and the model reads its input width from the embedding file.

quotes.text: (esm_320, esm_640, esm_1280, esmc_960, esmc_1152, deepfri_bp, deepfri_cc, deepfri_ec, deepfri_mf, prost_1024)

strengths.text: Hard splits are shipped, not just a random one: drug cold, protein cold and fully blind folds for both datasets, five of each.

strengths.text: Runs can be made deterministic: given a seed, the script seeds python, numpy and torch, sets the cublas workspace, turns cudnn benchmarking off and asks torch for deterministic algorithms.
The plain GraphDTA models are in the same codebase and the same training loop, so the comparison between a learned sequence encoder and a language model embedding is made under one harness.

It needs a GPU and a prior embedding pass. The training script uses CUDA mixed precision and 24 data loader workers by default, and the protein embeddings must be computed first with a separate script for each embedding type.

diagram.title: PLM-GraphDTA workflow
steps: protein sequences are embedded once by a protein language model and averaged over residues
the per protein vectors are stored in a json file
the drug graph is encoded by a GIN, GAT, GAT_GCN or GCN network
the protein vector passes through linear layers set by plm_layers
the two vectors are concatenated and sent through dense layers
output: one affinity value, scored by RMSE, MSE, Pearson, Spearman and CI
diagram.caption: The language model runs before training, not inside it, so the affinity model only ever sees one vector per protein.

run_guide.summary: Compute the ESM-2 protein embeddings for a dataset, then train and evaluate one PLM-GraphDTA variant on it.
prerequisites: The repository gives no environment file, so the dependencies have to be read from the imports: torch with CUDA, torch_geometric, fair-esm, rdkit, networkx, pandas, numpy, tqdm and wandb.
A CUDA GPU. The training script uses mixed precision through torch.cuda.amp and the embedding script moves the language model to the GPU when one is present.
No data download: the Davis and KIBA drug, protein and fold files are in the repository.
No licence is declared for the code or the shipped data.

steps.title: Compute the protein embeddings
steps.explanation: The script loops over the davis, kiba and davis_mutation datasets, embeds each protein with esm2_t30_150M_UR50D, averages the last layer over the residues and writes data/<dataset>/proteins_esm_<width>.json. The file name carries the embedding width, which is what the training argument then refers to. The script takes no arguments in the version read.

steps.title: Train and evaluate one configuration
steps.shell: python training.py --dataset davis --model PLM_GINConvNet --protein_embedding_type esm_640 --plm_layers 128 --fold_setting setting1 --seed 42 --cuda 0
steps.explanation: The flags are the ones training.py's argument parser defines, with values from the help strings: a dataset name, a model from the table in the script, an embedding type, the widths of the protein branch, a fold setting and a seed. The embedding type must match a proteins_<type>.json file produced by the previous step, so set it to the width that step printed.

notes: This record's existing source, the Marijan and Tanasijevic 2026 preprint (doi 10.64898/2026.08.31.748056), is the study this repository belongs to: the repository description names the same title. The preprint is bioRxiv only (pdf at https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.08.31.748056v1.full.pdf) and was not fetched in this pass, so the page is written from the code alone and coverage is limited. Two things a reviewer may want to check against the preprint: the training script selects its checkpoint on training loss rather than a validation split, and the ESM preprocessing script as committed uses esm2_t30_150M_UR50D with two larger models commented out, while the training argument offers esm_320, esm_640 and esm_1280 widths. The repository also contains an esm_gat model and ESM Cambrian, DeepFRI and ProstT5 preprocessing scripts that were not read. Sibling record DeepGraphDTA from the same preprint has no file of that name in this repository and was left as a stub.
